title: Back to the Future's refrigerator time machine
hook: Before it was a DeLorean, Back to the Future's time machine was a fridge.
peek: In early drafts of Back to the Future, Doc Brown's time machine was not a sports car but a refrigerator. The filmmakers dropped it partly because they worried children might copy the film and shut themselves inside real fridges.
lede: Robert Zemeckis and Bob Gale spent years writing Back to the Future, released in 1985. In early drafts Doc Brown's time machine was not a car at all. For a while it was a refrigerator. Marty would climb inside and travel through time. By the time filming began the fridge was gone, replaced by a stainless steel DeLorean sports car.

bullets.text: Zemeckis has said one reason for dropping the fridge was the fear that children would imitate the film. Old refrigerators that latched from the outside were a known hazard, and nobody wanted a scene that encouraged climbing into one.

A car could move, which made the time travel more exciting. Zemeckis also liked that the DeLorean's gull-wing doors made it look like a spaceship, so the 1955 farm family who find it could mistake it for a flying saucer.
Making the machine a car gave the film its rule that the DeLorean must reach 88 miles per hour to jump through time. Bob Gale has said they picked the number simply because it was easy to remember.

The fridge idea did not vanish. Steven Spielberg, an executive producer on Back to the Future, later directed 2008's Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull, where Indy shelters inside a refrigerator, a scene often seen as a nod to the old draft.
